content: Hypophyseal hypertrophy in pregnancy is a condition characterized by the enlargement of the pituitary gland during gestation. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) studies have demonstrated that the pituitary gland undergoes an approximate 30% increase in volume during pregnancy. This enlargement often results in an upward bulging of the gland. However, such complications are uncommon. Following delivery, the pituitary gland typically returns to its normal size. Despite the hyperplastic changes observed in the pituitary gland during pregnancy, there is no evidence to suggest an increased risk of developing pituitary tumors, such as prolactinomas, as a result of this physiological adaptation.
